audits.title: Comparison of appropriateness of cholesterol testing in general practice with the recommendations of national guidelines: an audit of patient records in 20 general practices.

cycle1.result: Cholesterol tested in 415 (11.7%); only 31% of 668 patients with a positive cardiovascular risk profile tested, versus 8% of those without.

audits.title: Reducing unnecessary blood work in the neurosurgical ICU.
audits.standard: Blood work should match physicians' orders
audits.setting: Neurosurgical intensive care unit, Hartford Hospital, urban teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Blood drawn without orders, duplicate tests and blood work continuing long past medical need.

audits.intervention: In-service training, reminder posters, protocol reference sheets and medical staff memoranda; further measures after repeat audits.

cycle2.result: Project goals were met; unordered blood work reduced (no figures given).

audits.other_findings: Identifying the time of day of requests and who sent unordered tests helped reduce them.
audits.citation: Beland D, D'Angelo C, Vinci D. Reducing unnecessary blood work in the neurosurgical ICU. J Neurosci Nurs. 2003;35(3):149-152. doi:10.1097/01376517-200306000-00004. PMID: 12830662.

audits.title: An audit of 24-hour creatinine clearance measurements at Tygerberg Hospital and comparison with prediction equations.
audits.standard: Clinical guidelines recommending creatinine-based eGFR equations instead of routine 24-hour creatinine clearance
audits.setting: Tygerberg Hospital chemical pathology, Western Cape

cycle1.result: Problems with urine collection or data supplied in one third of creatinine clearance requests, giving unreliable results.

audits.title: Targeted thyroid testing in acute illness: achieving success through audit.
audits.setting: Medical Assessment Unit, Caerphilly Miners' Hospital

cycle1.result: 53.8% of admissions had thyroid tests; appropriate indications documented in 43.9% of those with abnormal results; intervention documented in 25.5% and follow-up in 45.5%.

audits.intervention: Guidelines on indications for thyroid testing were issued.

cycle2.result: Thyroid testing fell to 21.7% (p<0.001); appropriate indications documented in 73.7% of abnormal results (p=0.004); intervention documentation 92.9% and follow-up 85.7% (p=0.001).

audits.other_findings: Indications in a random sample of normal results barely changed (14.3% vs 16%, p=0.77).
audits.citation: Adlan MA, Neel V, Lakra SS, Bondugulapati LN, Premawardhana LD. Targeted thyroid testing in acute illness: achieving success through audit. J Endocrinol Invest. 2011;34(8):e210-3. doi:10.3275/7480. PMID: 21270508.

audits.title: Improving serological test ordering patterns for the diagnosis of celiac disease through clinical laboratory audit of practice.
audits.standard: Clinical practice guidelines recommending tTG to screen for coeliac disease

cycle1.result: Coeliac panel ordered in 48.4% of children and 72.3% of adults; tTG alone in 7.2% of adults.

audits.intervention: Interaction with physicians, revised test menu and changed test ordering policy.

cycle2.result: Coeliac panel 3.6% in children and 28.1% in adults; tTG alone over 90% in children and 61.3% in adults.

audits.other_findings: In adults tTG alone rose from 8.9% to 63.9% for gastroenterologists and 8.1% to 44.4% for other physicians.

audits.title: An audit of the laboratory diagnosis of cryptosporidiosis in England and Wales.
audits.standard: UK national standards for Cryptosporidium testing
audits.setting: Publicly funded clinical microbiology laboratories in England and Wales

cycle1.result: 85/156 (54%) laboratories responded; first-line methods microscopy 68/85 (80%), EIA 16/85 (19%), PCR 1/85 (1%); 28/85 (33%) routinely tested all stools; 16 (19%) used stool consistency to select samples.

audits.other_findings: Other selection criteria included age (21%), clinical details (47%), hospitalisation duration (21%) and clinician request (29%); national standard revision under way to encourage testing all stools.

audits.title: Reducing the number of unnecessary liver function tests requested on the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Blood tests requested according to previous results and clinical condition
audits.setting: Paediatric Intensive Care Unit, Great Ormond Street Hospital

cycle1.result: LFTs requested daily on most patients, even with previous normal results; average blood test spend £23,392 per month.

audits.intervention: Blood test request form to document nurse-doctor discussion, with two nurse champions providing bedside support, education and feedback, via PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Significant sustained reduction in LFT requests, with similar reductions in FBC, coagulation screens and CRP.

audits.citation: Sinitsky L, Brierley J. Reducing the number of unnecessary liver function tests requested on the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2017;6(1):u214071.w5561. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u214071.w5561. PMID: 28674611.

audits.title: Reducing waste: a guidelines-based approach to reducing inappropriate vitamin D and TSH testing in the inpatient rehabilitation setting.
audits.standard: Discipline-specific guidelines not supporting routine admission testing; target 25% reduction
audits.setting: Inpatient rehabilitation units, London Health Sciences Centre, Ontario

cycle1.result: 94% of patients had vitamin D and TSH tests on admission; 100% (n=6) of admission order sets prepopulated.

audits.intervention: Academic detailing, computerised clinical decision support limiting vitamin D testing, removal of automatic orders, and audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Vitamin D testing 2.9% (97% relative reduction); TSH testing 53% (43% relative reduction); prepopulated order sets 0%.

audits.other_findings: Decision support was more effective than education or feedback alone; over 9000 dollars annualised savings.
audits.citation: Bateman EA, Gob A, Chin-Yee I, MacKenzie HM. Reducing waste: a guidelines-based approach to reducing inappropriate vitamin D and TSH testing in the inpatient rehabilitation setting. BMJ Open Qual. 2019;8(4):e000674. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2019-000674. PMID: 31750404.

audits.title: Uses and misuses of serum hCG--a clinical audit.
audits.standard: Locally agreed clinical criteria for serum hCG requests
audits.setting: Clinical chemistry laboratory, City Hospital NHS Trust, Birmingham

cycle1.result: Only 35% of 142 requests conformed to agreed criteria; 49% (routine pregnancy diagnosis, threatened miscarriage, abdominal pain screen) seemed inappropriate.

audits.intervention: Criteria reinforced and re-issued to clinical teams; semi-quantitative urine hCG assay introduced in A&E for approved staff

cycle2.period: Six months after the service change
cycle2.result: No increase in hCG requests compared with the preceding half year; 208 (26%) urine tests unaccounted for, eroding theoretical savings of 5173 pounds per annum by about 10%.

audits.other_findings: Workload had risen by 309% between 1988 and 1992; no pregnancy was diagnosed by abdominal pain screen.
audits.citation: Magnay JL, Bayly GR. Uses and misuses of serum hCG--a clinical audit. Br J Biomed Sci. 1995;52(1):26-30. PMID: 7549603.

audits.title: Computer-based audit to detect and correct overutilization of laboratory tests.
audits.standard: Explicit criteria justifying three or more LDH or calcium tests in seven days

cycle1.result: 51% of charts with repeated LDH showed overutilisation.

audits.intervention: Physicians notified of overutilisation found by computer-based audit, with education.

cycle2.result: 65% of charts showed overutilisation (not significant); undisclosed calcium audit also unchanged.

audits.other_findings: Detection method worked but notification and education did not reduce overuse.

audits.title: Reducing redundant creatine kinase testing in cardiac injury.
audits.standard: Choosing Wisely and cardiology society guidance that troponin alone is the biomarker of choice for cardiac injury; target 50% reduction in CK tests and CK-to-troponin ratio of one-third or less
audits.setting: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre, large academic cardiac centre, Toronto

cycle1.result: 47,556 CK tests (mean 3963 per month); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.91; 72.8% of CK tests coupled with troponin.

audits.intervention: Revised institutional testing guidelines; CK removed from ED triage, cardiology admission, cardiovascular surgery and ICU order sets; academic detailing and education; unit-level comparative feedback by email; reduced default intervals for recurring CK tests.

cycle2.result: 25,332 CK tests (mean 2111 per month), a 46.7% reduction (p<0.001); CK-to-troponin ratio 0.49; coupled tests 58.3% of CK orders.

audits.other_findings: Troponin testing did not change; the reduction was sustained in January to March 2020 and projected annual savings were C$28,446. The 50% target was narrowly missed.
audits.citation: Raza S, Amaral AC, Pang J, Moussa F, Shelton D, Notario L, et al.. Reducing redundant creatine kinase testing in cardiac injury. BMJ Open Qual. 2020;9(4):e001182. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2020-001182. PMID: 33376105.
